formulation_b_gauss_point.description: Turn 315 Python Gauss-point interpolated degradation g(d_g)

h48_phase_only.driving_history: Transferred donor H0 from C3 (near equilibrium)

h49_coupled_am.driving_history: Refined C4 singular strain concentration psi_e^+ (+150% above H0)

findings.detail: Formulation A (element-average degradation g(d_avg), as defined in f42_mixed_uel.for lines 408-410) matches authentic Abaqus Package 142 to within 0.0002% in RF2 (194.1213 N vs 194.1213 N) and 0.0001% in elastic energy (0.174740 mJ vs 0.174740 mJ).

Formulation B (Turn 315 Python Gauss-point degradation g(d_g)) exhibits a slight stiffening shift of -0.0195% in RF2 and -0.0198% in elastic energy relative to authentic Abaqus UEL, governed by Jensen's inequality for convex (1-d)^2 over intra-element phase gradients.

H48 uncoupled phase relaxation was evaluated under frozen donor history H0 from C3, where driving force was small (Delta d_max = 0.007630). H49 coupled relaxation solved mechanical displacements on the refined C4 mesh (h_tip = 0.6 um), capturing the notch-tip singular strain concentration psi_e^+ which exceeded H0 by +150% and drove physically admissible crack growth (Delta d_max = 0.09105, Delta E_frac = +20.30%).

Coupled material softening relaxed elastic strain energy by -0.008324 mJ (-4.76%), compensating 95.3% of the fracture dissipation increase (+0.007935 mJ). Net total energy relaxed by only -0.000390 mJ (-0.1822%), mathematically proving that coupled PDAS re-equilibration cannot bridge the +2.43% refinement energy excess.

Evaluated against authentic Package 143 Frame-77 baseline (RF2 = 188.4570 N, E_tot = 0.208752 mJ), coupled PDAS yields RF2 error -1.9214% (PASS <= 5.0%) but total energy error +2.2310% (FAILS <= 2.000%). Stage C1-1 remains failed.

Authentic Abaqus coupled PDAS requires an external iterative loop to update active sets between subproblems. Submitting a single static .inp to PBS would replicate Package 142's clamped linear elastic run. Submission withheld pursuant to policy.
